blocks.text: Validation checks how well a model works on new data, after training and testing, to confirm that it is reliable. It stops the model from simply memorising its data and supports fair evaluation; the feedback from validation shows which areas to improve before the model is used for real.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Validation checks how a model works on new data and prevents overfitting; tuning and adjustments then improve the model, and good validation makes it reliable in real conditions.

items: Validation dataset: kept separate from the training and test data and used to check performance. It must be clean and represent real conditions; the model does not learn from it. It helps detect overfitting and makes the evaluation more trustworthy.

Robustness and reliability: a robust model performs well in different situations, handles noise in the data and does not fail with small changes; a reliable model gives consistent results. Testing under different conditions checks this, and it builds trust in the system.

Hyperparameter tuning: adjusting the model's settings (hyperparameters), which control how it learns, by trying different values and comparing them on validation data. Good tuning improves accuracy and reduces errors; poor tuning makes the model less effective.

blocks.title: Analogy: the volume of a speaker
blocks.text: Hyperparameter tuning is like setting a speaker's volume. Too high and the sound is distorted; too low and it cannot be heard; at the right level it is clear and balanced. In the same way, badly set hyperparameters make a model perform poorly, and the right values help it learn well and predict accurately.
